+# ===========================================================================
+# 19 — Consuming the portable `List` prelude (higher-order, closures-as-values)
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: real application code that USES the `List` combinators from the
+# portable prelude — `map`/`filter`/`reduce`/`member` — by passing closures.
+# This is the consumer side of ADR-0061's closure-as-value lowering: each `Fn`
+# callback flows into a prelude HOF and the whole thing stays portable across
+# every Tier-1 target.
+#
+#   List.map(xs, (x) -> e)      Elixir: Enum.map      Rust: map(xs, &|x| e)
+#   List.filter(xs, (x) -> p)   a `&impl Fn(T) -> Bool` on Rust
+#   List.reduce(xs, acc, f)     a `&impl Fn(T, U) -> U`, accumulator threaded
+#
+# Every function below reaches `:ex`, `:rs`, and `:js` — `mix rian.targets`
+# proves it (the prelude calls are portable, the closures lower per target).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# map — double every element via a one-arg closure.
+pub def doubled(xs Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53) := List.map(xs, (x) -> x * 2)
+
+# filter — keep the evens via a `Fn(Int53, Bool)` predicate.
+pub def evens(xs Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53) := List.filter(xs, (x) -> x rem 2 == 0)
+
+# reduce — sum via a `Fn(Int53, Int53, Int53)` folding closure (element, acc -> acc).
+pub def total(xs Vec(Int53)) Int53 := List.reduce(xs, 0, (x, acc) -> x + acc)
+
+# member — `Eq`-based membership (no closure; `T: Eq` is `RianEq` on Rust).
+pub def has(xs Vec(Int53), n Int53) Bool := List.member(xs, n)
+
+# Composed pipeline: double, keep evens, then sum — three closures, one portable
+# expression. (`doubled`/`evens` already produce owned `Vec`s the next call borrows.)
+pub def sum_of_doubled_evens(xs Vec(Int53)) Int53 := total(evens(doubled(xs)))

       assert mod.max() == 99

+    test "the prelude-consumer tour example runs on BEAM (List HOF fed closures, ADR-0061)" do
+      src = File.read!("examples/rian/19_prelude_consumer.rian")
+      {:ok, mod} = Beam.load(src, :"Elixir.RianPreludeConsumer19")
+
+      assert mod.doubled([1, 2, 3, 4]) == [2, 4, 6, 8]
+      assert mod.evens([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) == [2, 4, 6]
+      assert mod.total([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 10
+      assert mod.has([1, 2, 3], 2) == true
+      assert mod.has([1, 2, 3], 9) == false
+      assert mod.sum_of_doubled_evens([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 20
+
+      # the consumer is portable — every function reaches the shared core (ADR-0061)
+      rep = src |> Rian.Decl.parse() |> Rian.Reach.analyze()
+
+      for f <- ~w(doubled evens total has sum_of_doubled_evens) do
+        assert :rs in (rep[f].reach |> MapSet.to_list()), "#{f} should reach :rs"
+      end
+    end
